speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. You presented with sudden-onset vertigo; to begin our assessment, have you experienced any headache, double vision, slurred speech, or weakness in your limbs?

speaker: Patient
text: 59-year-old male. The patient presents to the emergency department with a sudden-onset sensation that the room is spinning, leading to several episodes of nausea and vomiting. The symptoms started as he was going to bed and lasted for approximately 3 minutes. He mentions that he has never experienced anything like this before and currently feels at his baseline.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Thank you for the details. Since your vertigo was brief (3 minutes) and you have returned to your baseline without neurological deficits, was the episode triggered by a specific head movement, such as rolling over in bed or looking up?

REQUEST TEST: Electrocardiogram (to rule out cardiac arrhythmias as a cause of syncope or vertebrobasilar insufficiency).

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Sudden-onset sensation of the room spinning. I also have Nausea, Vomiting, Dizziness. I am scared this situation could become urgent and I need the most appropriate final answer immediately. Please do not wait too long before committing to a next step.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Benign Paroxysmal Positional Vertigo (BPPV)
